subject: Discovery: Nimbus Health - Private/VPC architecture review

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@nimbushealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: Nimbus Health - Private/VPC architecture review

Hi Daniel and Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today - really useful conversation. Quick recap from our discovery call:

- Goal: Evaluate Private deployment options for your PHI workloads (VPC + on-prem gateway) and ensure we meet Nimbus Health security controls and audit requirements.
- Top concerns: network isolation, customer-managed KMS, audit/log retention, and SSO provisioning.
- Expected scale: pilot ~2-4 GPU nodes, steady-state ~10-20 nodes; burst capacity discussed.

Next step: technical deep dive / architecture review to walk through our Private offering, network diagrams, and an onboarding checklist. Can we schedule a 60-75 minute call with your infra/security folks so Neha (our Solutions Engineer) can walk the design and Rishi (AE) can cover commercial checklist?

Proposed slots (PT):
- Tue Oct 5 - 10:00-11:15am PT
- Wed Oct 6 - 10:00-11:15am PT
- Wed Oct 6 - 3:00-4:15pm PT (if you need later in day)

If those don't work, send a few times that suit your network/security and I'll coordinate. Attached is a short pre-call checklist and a one-pager on our Private deployment to help your team prepare.

Attachments: nimbus_precall_checklist.pdf (PDF, 89 KB), redwood_private_deployment_onepager.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.co@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

--
Redwood Inference - developer-first inference platform for production LLMs

- Please include our Network engineer (Priya) and our Security lead (Daniel Liu) on the architecture call.
- Best slots for us are Tue Oct 5 after 9am PT or Wed Oct 6 morning - Wed 10am PT looks good.

Also: can you include a short section on expected firewall rules / ports and whether we need dedicated NAT/egress arrangements for telemetry?
